data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"There are 648 three-digit numbers (100 to 999) with all distinct digits, computed via casework on zero: 144 have zero (with 1-9 in hundreds, 8 options in the remaining nonzero slot), plus 504 have no zero (9*8*7 choices), giving 144 + 504 = 648.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If zero appearing in tens or units still triggered an extra adjacency restriction, the 144 count would not hold.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If 'three-digit number' excluded any number containing the digit zero (contrary to standard conventions), only case B would survive and the answer would be 504.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the problem instead required 'all digits nonzero' rather than 'all three digits different', the count would be 504 and the 144 zero-cases would be invalid.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Split all valid numbers by whether zero appears. (A) Zero appears: hundreds digit has 9 options (1-9); exactly one of tens or units is zero (2 positions); the other nonzero digit has 8 options. Count: 9*2*8 = 144. (B) No zero appears: choose hundreds (9 options 1-9), tens (8 remaining nonzero), units (7 remaining nonzero). Count: 9*8*7 = 504.
